paper.title: UP TGT Mathematics 2021
paper.source: UPSESSB TGT written examination 2021, Mathematics, booklet TG-06 series D (question booklet as shared after the exam; booklet page 11, questions 34 to 38, is missing from the available copy)
paper.note: Questions 34 to 38 are missing from the only available copy of the booklet.

en.q: If $y = \log_5 x + \log_x 5$, then what will be the value of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = 5$?
en.explanation: Write $y = \dfrac{\ln x}{\ln 5} + \dfrac{\ln 5}{\ln x}$. Then $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{x\ln 5} - \dfrac{\ln 5}{x(\ln x)^2}$. At $x = 5$: $\dfrac{1}{5\ln 5} - \dfrac{\ln 5}{5(\ln 5)^2} = 0$.
notes: Only the derivative of the first term, $\frac{1}{x\ln 5}$, with $\ln 5$ dropped.
Correct: $y = t + \frac1t$ with $t = \log_5 x$, and $t = 1$ at $x = 5$ is its minimum.
facts: $\log_5 x + \log_x 5 = t + \frac{1}{t}$ is stationary where $t = 1$, i.e. at $x = 5$.

en.q: The minimum value of $4\cos\theta + 3$ is
en.explanation: Since $-1 \le \cos\theta \le 1$, the least value is $4(-1) + 3 = -1$ (at $\theta = \pi$).
notes: Needs $\cos\theta = -\frac34$; a value, not the least.
$\cos\theta = -\frac12$ gives 1; a value, not the least.
facts: $a\cos\theta + c$ ranges over $[c - |a|,\ c + |a|]$.

en.q: A force represented by $\hat i + 2\hat j + \hat k$ passes through a point $(2, 3, 1)$. The moment of the force about point $(1, 2, -1)$ is
en.explanation: $\vec r = (2,3,1) - (1,2,-1) = \hat i + \hat j + 2\hat k$. Moment $= \vec r \times \vec F = \begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\1&1&2\\1&2&1\end{vmatrix} = (1-4)\hat i - (1-2)\hat j + (2-1)\hat k = -3\hat i + \hat j + \hat k$.
notes: This is $\vec F \times \vec r$: the order is reversed; it must be $\vec r \times \vec F$.
Sign errors in the cross product.
facts: Moment about $B$ of a force $\vec F$ acting at $A$: $\overrightarrow{BA} \times \vec F$.

en.q: Sum of the series $2 + \frac{3}{2} + 1 + \frac{5}{8} + \cdots \infty$ is
en.explanation: The terms are $\frac{2}{1}, \frac{3}{2}, \frac{4}{4}, \frac{5}{8}, \dots$, i.e. $\dfrac{k+2}{2^k}$ for $k = 0, 1, 2, \dots$ (an AGP). So $S = \sum \dfrac{k}{2^k} + 2\sum \dfrac{1}{2^k} = 2 + 2\cdot 2 = 6$.
notes: Only $2\sum 2^{-k} = 4$; the $\sum k/2^k$ part is missed.
path: 1.6 Sequences and series: AP, GP, HP
facts: $\sum_{k\ge0} k x^k = \dfrac{x}{(1-x)^2}$; at $x = \tfrac12$ it is 2.

en.q: A stone thrown up is caught by the thrower after 6 sec. What will be the velocity of stone after 2 sec of its throwing? ($g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$)
en.explanation: Up and down take 3 s each, so $u = g \cdot 3 = 29.4$ m/s. After 2 s: $v = u - gt = 29.4 - 19.6 = 9.8$ m/s (still rising).
notes: This is $g t$ for $t = 2$, the speed lost, not the speed left.
path: 15.8 Rectilinear motion and simple harmonic motion
facts: Time of flight $T = 2u/g$, so $u = gT/2$.

en.q: The area cut off the parabola $4y = 3x^2$ by the straight line $2y = 3x + 12$ is
notes: Correct; shortcut: for $y = ax^2$ cut by a chord, area $= \frac{a}{6}(x_2 - x_1)^3 = \frac{3/4}{6}\cdot 216 = 27$.
facts: Area between $y = ax^2$ and a chord with ends at $x_1, x_2$: $\frac{a}{6}(x_2 - x_1)^3$.

en.q: In the following figure AD is tangent of the circle and ABC is secant. If $AB = 4$ cm and $BC = 5$ cm, then the length of tangent AD is (figure: secant from A meets the circle at B then C; AD touches the circle at D)
en.explanation: Tangent–secant theorem: $AD^2 = AB \cdot AC = 4 \times (4 + 5) = 36$, so $AD = 6$ cm.
notes: That is $BC$; the tangent needs $AD^2 = AB \cdot AC$, not $BC$.
facts: Square of the tangent = (whole secant) × (external part).

en.q: If $\vec A$ and $\vec B$ are two vectors, then angle between vectors $\vec A + \vec B$ and $\vec A \times \vec B$ is
en.explanation: $\vec A \times \vec B$ is perpendicular to both $\vec A$ and $\vec B$, hence to $\vec A + \vec B$: $(\vec A + \vec B)\cdot(\vec A \times \vec B) = 0$. The angle is $90^\circ$.
facts: $\vec A \times \vec B$ is normal to the plane of $\vec A$ and $\vec B$.

en.q: The distance of centre of gravity of uniform semicircular lamina of radius $a$, from the centre is
en.explanation: For a semicircular lamina $\bar y = \dfrac{\int y\,dA}{A} = \dfrac{\frac23 a^3}{\frac12\pi a^2} = \dfrac{4a}{3\pi}$.
facts: C.G. from the centre: semicircular arc $\frac{2a}{\pi}$, semicircular lamina $\frac{4a}{3\pi}$, solid hemisphere $\frac{3a}{8}$.

en.q: If $f(x) = \tan^{-1}x$ and $g(x) = \sin x$, then $(g \circ f)(x)$ is equal to
en.explanation: $(g\circ f)(x) = \sin(\tan^{-1}x)$. If $\tan\theta = x$ with $\theta \in (-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2})$, a right triangle with sides $x, 1, \sqrt{1+x^2}$ gives $\sin\theta = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}$.

en.q: A body is projected with velocity 40 metre per second inclined at an angle $60^\circ$ with horizontal. The velocity of the body when it is at maximum height is
en.explanation: At the top the vertical velocity is zero; only the horizontal part remains: $u\cos 60^\circ = 40 \cdot \frac12 = 20$ m/s.
facts: Speed at the highest point of a projectile $= u\cos\alpha$.

en.q: The value of $\dfrac{(x - y)^3 + (y - z)^3 + (z - x)^3}{9(x - y)(y - z)(z - x)}$ is
en.explanation: Put $a = x - y$, $b = y - z$, $c = z - x$; then $a + b + c = 0$, so $a^3 + b^3 + c^3 = 3abc$. The value is $\dfrac{3abc}{9abc} = \dfrac13$.
facts: If $a + b + c = 0$ then $a^3 + b^3 + c^3 = 3abc$.

en.q: The order of the differential equation $y - x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 = a\left(y^2 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right)$ is
en.explanation: Only the first derivative $\frac{dy}{dx}$ occurs, so the order is 1 (its degree is 3).
notes: That is the degree (highest power of $dy/dx$), not the order.
A power of 2 is not a second derivative.
facts: Order = highest derivative present; degree = power of that derivative.

en.q: $\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/3} \frac{dx}{\sin^2 x\cos^2 x}$ is equal to
en.explanation:
$\dfrac{1}{\sin^2x\cos^2x} = \dfrac{\sin^2x + \cos^2x}{\sin^2x\cos^2x} = \sec^2x + \csc^2x$, whose antiderivative is $\tan x - \cot x$.
$$\Big[\tan x - \cot x\Big]_{\pi/4}^{\pi/3} = \Big(\sqrt3 - \tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\Big) - (1 - 1) = \tfrac{2}{\sqrt3}.$$
facts: $\int \frac{dx}{\sin^2x\cos^2x} = \tan x - \cot x + C$.

en.q: A person travels from A to B at a speed of 40 kmph and returns by increasing his speed by 50%. What is his average speed for both the trips?
en.explanation: Return speed $= 60$ kmph. For equal distances the average speed is the harmonic mean: $\dfrac{2 \cdot 40 \cdot 60}{40 + 60} = 48$ kmph.
notes: The arithmetic mean of 40 and 60, wrong for equal distances.
facts: Equal distances at speeds $u, v$: average speed $= \frac{2uv}{u+v}$.

en.q: If $x_1$ and $x_2$ are roots of $x^2 - 2x + 4 = 0$, then the value of $x_1^3 + x_2^3$ is equal to
path: 1.8 Quadratic equations and theory of equations
facts: $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = (\alpha+\beta)^3 - 3\alpha\beta(\alpha+\beta)$.

en.q: The speeds of three cars are in the ratio $2 : 3 : 4$. The ratios of the times taken by these cars in travelling 100 km distance will be
en.explanation: For a fixed distance, time $\propto \frac{1}{\text{speed}}$: $\frac12 : \frac13 : \frac14 = 6 : 4 : 3$ (multiply by 12).
notes: Reverses the order but does not invert.
facts: Same distance: times are in the inverse ratio of the speeds.

en.q: $\int \frac{e^x(x - 1)}{(x + 1)^3}\,dx$ equals to
en.explanation: $\dfrac{x - 1}{(x+1)^3} = \dfrac{(x+1) - 2}{(x+1)^3} = \dfrac{1}{(x+1)^2} - \dfrac{2}{(x+1)^3} = f(x) + f'(x)$ with $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{(x+1)^2}$. Since $\int e^x\{f + f'\}dx = e^x f + C$, the answer is $\dfrac{e^x}{(x+1)^2} + C$.
facts: $\int e^x\{f(x) + f'(x)\}\,dx = e^x f(x) + C$.

en.q: If $i = \sqrt{-1}$, then $(1 + i)^4 - (1 - i)^4$ is equal to
What is the real part of $(\sin x + i\cos x)^4$, $i = \sqrt{-1}$?
en.explanation: $\sin x + i\cos x = i(\cos x - i\sin x) = i e^{-ix}$. So the fourth power is $i^4 e^{-4ix} = \cos 4x - i\sin 4x$, real part $\cos 4x$.
path: 10.4 Polar form, Euler's form and De Moivre's theorem
facts: $\sin x + i\cos x = i(\cos x - i\sin x)$; then use De Moivre.

en.q: If $A = \begin{bmatrix}1&-2\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix}2&6\\1&3\end{bmatrix}$, then $AB$ is equal to
en.explanation: Row 1: $(1\cdot2 - 2\cdot1,\ 1\cdot6 - 2\cdot3) = (0, 0)$. Row 2: $(-2 + 2,\ -6 + 6) = (0, 0)$. So $AB = O$ although $A, B \neq O$.
facts: A product of two non-zero matrices can be the zero matrix.

en.q: Equation of a circle, with center $(0, 0)$ and $2x + 3y = 5$ as a tangent, is
en.explanation: Radius = distance of the centre from the tangent $= \dfrac{|0 + 0 - 5|}{\sqrt{4 + 9}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{13}}$. So $x^2 + y^2 = \dfrac{25}{13}$, i.e. $13x^2 + 13y^2 = 25$.
facts: Radius of a circle touching a line = perpendicular distance of the centre from it.

en.q: The order of the element $(-i)$ of the multiplicative group $G = \{1, -1, i, -i\}$ is
The value of $n$, for which $\dfrac{a^{n+1} + b^{n+1}}{a^n + b^n}$ is the harmonic mean of $a$ and $b$, is
en.explanation: For $n = -1$: $\dfrac{1 + 1}{\frac1a + \frac1b} = \dfrac{2ab}{a + b}$, the HM.
notes: Sign slip: it is $n = -\frac12$ that gives the GM, $\sqrt{ab}$.
path: 1.6 Sequences and series: AP, GP, HP
facts: $\frac{a^{n+1}+b^{n+1}}{a^n+b^n}$ is the AM for $n = 0$, GM for $n = -\frac12$, HM for $n = -1$.

en.q: If $x + \dfrac{1}{x} = 2\cos\dfrac{\pi}{5}$, then $x^5 + \dfrac{1}{x^5}$ is equal to
en.explanation: $x = \cos\frac{\pi}{5} \pm i\sin\frac{\pi}{5}$. By De Moivre $x^5 + x^{-5} = 2\cos\left(5 \cdot \frac{\pi}{5}\right) = 2\cos\pi = -2$.
path: 10.4 Polar form, Euler's form and De Moivre's theorem
facts: If $x + \frac1x = 2\cos\theta$ then $x^n + \frac{1}{x^n} = 2\cos n\theta$.

en.q: Three forces $P$, $2P$ and $3P$ are acting along sides AB, BC and CA of equilateral $\triangle ABC$. Magnitude of resultant force is
en.explanation:
Take AB along $0^\circ$; then BC is along $120^\circ$ and CA along $240^\circ$. Equal $P$'s around the triangle cancel, leaving $P$ along BC and $2P$ along CA, at $120^\circ$ to each other.
$$R^2 = P^2 + 4P^2 + 2\cdot P\cdot 2P\cos120^\circ = 3P^2 \Rightarrow R = P\sqrt3.$$
notes: Only if the three forces were equal.
facts: Equal forces taken in order round a triangle are in equilibrium; subtract that part first.

en.q: If $y = x^x$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ will be
en.explanation: $\log y = x\log x \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \log x + 1$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x^x(1 + \log x)$.
facts: $\frac{d}{dx}x^x = x^x(1 + \log x)$ (logarithmic differentiation).

en.q: If the probability for A to fail in an examination is 0.20 and that of B to fail is 0.30, then the probability that either A or B fails is
en.explanation: The question does not say so, but the results are meant to be independent: $P(A \cup B) = 0.2 + 0.3 - 0.2 \times 0.3 = 0.44$. (Equivalently $1 - 0.8 \times 0.7 = 0.44$.)
notes: Adds the probabilities as if the events were mutually exclusive.
path: 16.2 Conditional probability, multiplication theorem, independent events
facts: $P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - P(\bar A)P(\bar B)$ for independent events.

en.q: The distances travelled by a body falling freely from rest in the first, second and third second are in the ratio
en.explanation: Distance in the $n$th second from rest: $s_n = \frac{g}{2}(2n - 1)$, giving $1 : 3 : 5$.
notes: Ratio of total distances after 1, 2, 3 s.
path: 15.8 Rectilinear motion and simple harmonic motion
facts: From rest, distances in successive equal intervals are as the odd numbers 1 : 3 : 5 : ….

en.q: A sum becomes double in 5 years in C.I. When will it become 8 times at the same rate of interest?
facts: Under C.I., doubling in $T$ years means $2^k$ times in $kT$ years.

en.q: The smallest positive integer $n$ for which $\left(\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i}\right)^n = 1$, is
en.explanation: $\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i} = \dfrac{(1 + i)^2}{2} = i$, and $i^n = 1$ first for $n = 4$.
notes: A multiple of 4, not the smallest.

en.q: If 3 men working 3 hours per day make 3 toys in 3 days, then the number of toys which can be made by 6 men working 6 hours per day in 6 days is
en.explanation: Toys $\propto$ men × hours/day × days. Each factor doubles, so toys $= 3 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 24$.

en.q: In a $\triangle ABC$, $b = 5$ cm, $a = 2$ cm and $\sin A = \dfrac{3}{7}$. How many such triangles are possible?
en.explanation: Sine rule: $\sin B = \dfrac{b\sin A}{a} = \dfrac{5 \cdot 3/7}{2} = \dfrac{15}{14} > 1$. Impossible, so no triangle.
facts: Given $a, b, A$: no triangle if $a < b\sin A$, one if $a = b\sin A$ or $a \ge b$, two if $b\sin A < a < b$ (with $A$ acute).

en.q: If $A$ and $B$ are two matrices such that $AB = B$ and $BA = A$, then $A^2 + B^2$ is equal to
en.explanation: $A^2 = A\cdot A = A(BA) = (AB)A = BA = A$. Likewise $B^2 = B(AB) = (BA)B = AB = B$. So $A^2 + B^2 = A + B$.
facts: $AB = B,\ BA = A \Rightarrow A^2 = A,\ B^2 = B$.

en.q: If $A + iB = \tan(x + iy)$, then $\tan 2x$ is equal to
en.explanation: Conjugate: $\tan(x - iy) = A - iB$. Then $\tan 2x = \tan[(x + iy) + (x - iy)] = \dfrac{(A + iB) + (A - iB)}{1 - (A + iB)(A - iB)} = \dfrac{2A}{1 - A^2 - B^2}$.
path: 10.8 Separation into real and imaginary parts
facts: Write $2x = (x + iy) + (x - iy)$ and use the $\tan(\alpha+\beta)$ formula.

en.q: The term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(2x + \dfrac{1}{3x}\right)^6$ is
en.explanation: $T_{r+1} = \binom{6}{r}(2x)^{6-r}(3x)^{-r}$; the power of $x$ is $6 - 2r = 0 \Rightarrow r = 3$. $T_4 = 20 \cdot \dfrac{8}{27} = \dfrac{160}{27}$.
facts: In $(ax + \frac{b}{x})^{2m}$ the term free of $x$ is the middle one, $\binom{2m}{m}a^m b^m$.

en.q: Two consecutive sides of a parallelogram are $4x + 5y = 0$ and $7x + 2y = 0$. If the equation of one diagonal is $11x + 7y = 9$, the equation of other diagonal is
en.explanation: The sides meet at the origin O. The diagonal $11x + 7y = 9$ cuts them at $B(\frac53, -\frac43)$ and $D(-\frac23, \frac73)$. The diagonals bisect each other, so the other diagonal joins O to the midpoint $(\frac12, \frac12)$ of BD: $y = x$, i.e. $x - y = 0$.
facts: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.

en.q: The number of real solutions of the equation $|x|^2 - 3|x| + 2 = 0$ is
en.explanation: Put $t = |x| \ge 0$: $t^2 - 3t + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow t = 1, 2$. So $x = \pm1, \pm2$: four solutions.
path: 1.8 Quadratic equations and theory of equations
facts: Each positive root of the equation in $|x|$ gives two values of $x$.

en.q: If the foci of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$ and the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{144} - \dfrac{y^2}{81} = \dfrac{1}{25}$ coincide, then the value of $b^2$ is
en.explanation: Hyperbola: $\dfrac{x^2}{144/25} - \dfrac{y^2}{81/25} = 1$, so $c^2 = \dfrac{144 + 81}{25} = 9$, foci $(\pm3, 0)$. Ellipse: $16 - b^2 = 9 \Rightarrow b^2 = 7$.
facts: Foci: ellipse $c^2 = a^2 - b^2$; hyperbola $c^2 = a^2 + b^2$.

en.q: The general equation to the cone of second degree which passes through the axes, is
en.explanation: A cone with vertex O is $ax^2 + by^2 + cz^2 + 2fyz + 2gzx + 2hxy = 0$. The $x$-axis $(1, 0, 0)$ lies on it only if $a = 0$; similarly $b = c = 0$. What remains is $fyz + gzx + hxy = 0$.
notes: The axes lie on it only if $a = b = c = 0$.
facts: A cone through the three coordinate axes has no square terms: $fyz + gzx + hxy = 0$.

en.q: The point on the curve $y^2 = x$, the tangent at which makes an angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$ with $x$-axis, is
en.explanation: $2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2y} = \tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1 \Rightarrow y = \frac12$, $x = y^2 = \frac14$.
notes: Not on the curve ($x$ cannot be negative).
On the curve, but the slope there is $-1$.
facts: For $y^2 = 4ax$ the slope at $(x, y)$ is $2a/y$.

en.q: The points with position vectors $60\hat i + 3\hat j$, $40\hat i - 8\hat j$, $a\hat i - 52\hat j$ are collinear if $a$ is equal to
en.explanation: Slope through the first two points: $\dfrac{-8 - 3}{40 - 60} = \dfrac{11}{20}$. Through the 2nd and 3rd: $\dfrac{-52 + 8}{a - 40} = \dfrac{11}{20} \Rightarrow a - 40 = -80 \Rightarrow a = -40$.
facts: Three points are collinear when $\overrightarrow{AB} \parallel \overrightarrow{BC}$ (equal slopes).

en.q: In the equation $\cos^{-1}\dfrac{1 - a^2}{1 + a^2} - \cos^{-1}\dfrac{1 - b^2}{1 + b^2} = 2\tan^{-1}x$, value of $x$ is
en.explanation: For $a, b \ge 0$: $\cos^{-1}\dfrac{1 - a^2}{1 + a^2} = 2\tan^{-1}a$. So $2\tan^{-1}a - 2\tan^{-1}b = 2\tan^{-1}x$, giving $x = \tan(\tan^{-1}a - \tan^{-1}b) = \dfrac{a - b}{1 + ab}$.
notes: Would be the result for a sum.

en.q: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\tan(\cos^{-1}x)\right)^2$ is equal to
en.explanation: $\tan(\cos^{-1}x) = \dfrac{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}{x}$, so the function is $\dfrac{1 - x^2}{x^2} = x^{-2} - 1$. Its derivative is $-2x^{-3} = -\dfrac{2}{x^3}$.
facts: $\tan(\cos^{-1}x) = \frac{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}{x}$.

en.q: In a group of 300 people, 150 speak Hindi and 200 can speak English. How many can speak both Hindi and English?
en.explanation: Everyone speaks at least one language, so $n(H \cup E) = 300$. $n(H \cap E) = 150 + 200 - 300 = 50$.
facts: $n(A \cap B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cup B)$.

en.q: An aeroplane is flying at height $h$ with horizontal velocity $u$. The velocity of a dropped packet on reaching the ground will be
en.explanation: Horizontal velocity stays $u$; the vertical velocity gained in falling $h$ is $\sqrt{2gh}$. Resultant: $\sqrt{u^2 + 2gh}$.
facts: A dropped body keeps the horizontal velocity of its carrier.

en.q: A balloon is moving upward with uniform acceleration $\frac{g}{8}$ cm/sec$^2$. After half minute a body is dropped from them. The time taken by the body to reach on the ground is
en.explanation: Balloon starts from rest. At $t = 30$ s: $v = \frac{g}{8}\cdot30 = \frac{15g}{4}$ (upward), height $h = \frac12\cdot\frac{g}{8}\cdot900 = \frac{225g}{4}$. The body starts with $\frac{15g}{4}$ upward: $-\frac{225g}{4} = \frac{15g}{4}t - \frac{g}{2}t^2 \Rightarrow 2t^2 - 15t - 225 = 0 \Rightarrow (t - 15)(2t + 15) = 0$, so $t = 15$ s.
path: 15.8 Rectilinear motion and simple harmonic motion
facts: A body released from a moving balloon starts with the balloon's velocity, not from rest.

en.q: If three forces acting in one plane upon a rigid body, keep the body in equilibrium, then
options: They must meet in a point
They must either meet in a point or be parallel
en.explanation: If two of the forces meet, the third must pass through that point (moments about it vanish); if two are parallel, so is the third. Hence concurrent or parallel.
path: 15.2 Three forces in equilibrium: Lami's theorem
facts: Three coplanar forces in equilibrium are either concurrent or all parallel.

en.q: The equation $\dfrac{x^2}{1 - r} - \dfrac{y^2}{1 + r} = 1$, $|r| < 1$ represents
en.explanation: For $|r| < 1$ both $1 - r$ and $1 + r$ are positive, so this is $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$: a hyperbola.
notes: Needs a plus sign between the terms.
facts: $\frac{x^2}{A} - \frac{y^2}{B} = 1$ with $A, B > 0$ is a hyperbola.

en.q: How many words can be formed with the letters of the word 'POSTMAN', if every word begins with T and ends with M?
en.explanation: POSTMAN has 7 different letters. Fix T first and M last; the other 5 letters fill the middle in $5! = 120$ ways.
notes: Half of $5!$, as if a letter repeated.
facts: Fixing letters in places reduces the count to arrangements of the rest.

en.q: Function $f(x) = (x + 1)^{\cot x}$ will be continuous at $x = 0$ if the value of $f(0)$ is
en.explanation: $1^\infty$ form: $\lim_{x\to0}(1 + x)^{\cot x} = e^{\lim x\cot x} = e^{\lim \frac{x}{\tan x}} = e^1$. So $f(0) = e$.
facts: If $f \to 1$ and $g \to \infty$, then $\lim f^g = e^{\lim g(f - 1)}$.

en.q: If $z$ is a complex number of unit modulus and argument $\theta$, then $\arg\left(\dfrac{1 + z}{1 + \bar z}\right)$ is equal to
en.explanation: $|z| = 1 \Rightarrow \bar z = \frac{1}{z}$. Then $\dfrac{1 + z}{1 + \frac1z} = \dfrac{z(1 + z)}{z + 1} = z$, whose argument is $\theta$.
facts: On the unit circle $\bar z = 1/z$.

en.q: The area of the region bounded by the curves $y^2 = x$ and $x^2 = y$ is
en.explanation: They meet at $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$. Area $= \int_0^1(\sqrt x - x^2)\,dx = \frac23 - \frac13 = \frac13$.
facts: Area between $y^2 = 4ax$ and $x^2 = 4by$ is $\frac{16ab}{3}$.

en.q: $\lim_{x\to\infty}\left(\frac{x + 6}{x + 1}\right)^{x + 4}$ is equal to
en.explanation: $1^\infty$ form: $\lim (x + 4)\left(\dfrac{x + 6}{x + 1} - 1\right) = \lim \dfrac{5(x + 4)}{x + 1} = 5$. So the limit is $e^5$.
facts: $\lim\left(1 + \frac{a}{x}\right)^{x} = e^a$.

en.q: If the arithmetic mean from the following data is 21.5, the value of $k$ will be: $x$: 5, 15, 25, 35, 45; $f$: 6, 4, 3, $k$, 2
facts: Mean $= \frac{\sum f_i x_i}{\sum f_i}$.

en.q: $\int_1^3 (e^{\log x} + 1)\,dx$ is equal to
en.explanation: $e^{\log x} = x$, so the integral is $\left[\frac{x^2}{2} + x\right]_1^3 = 7.5 - 1.5 = 6$.
facts: $e^{\log x} = x$ for $x > 0$.

en.q: If for a moderately symmetrical distribution mean deviation is 12, then the value of standard deviation is
en.explanation: For a moderately symmetrical distribution, M.D. $\approx \frac45$ S.D. So S.D. $= \frac54 \times 12 = 15$.

en.q: If $\vec u = \hat i \times (\vec a \times \hat i) + \hat j \times (\vec a \times \hat j) + \hat k \times (\vec a \times \hat k)$ then $\vec u$ is equal to
en.explanation: $\hat i \times (\vec a \times \hat i) = \vec a(\hat i\cdot\hat i) - \hat i(\hat i\cdot\vec a) = \vec a - a_1\hat i$. Adding the three: $3\vec a - (a_1\hat i + a_2\hat j + a_3\hat k) = 2\vec a$.
notes: Forgets the $-(\hat i\cdot\vec a)\hat i$ parts.
facts: $\vec p \times (\vec q \times \vec r) = (\vec p\cdot\vec r)\vec q - (\vec p\cdot\vec q)\vec r$.

en.q: If the radius of a hemisphere is $a$, then its centre of gravity from its centre is at a distance
en.explanation: Solid hemisphere: slice into discs, $\bar z = \dfrac{\int_0^a z\,\pi(a^2 - z^2)\,dz}{\frac23\pi a^3} = \dfrac{\pi a^4/4}{\frac23\pi a^3} = \dfrac{3a}{8}$.
notes: That is for a hollow hemispherical shell.
facts: C.G.: solid hemisphere $\frac{3a}{8}$, hollow hemisphere $\frac{a}{2}$ from the centre.

en.q: If $\omega$ is an imaginary cube root of unity, then value of $\begin{vmatrix}1&\omega^6&\omega^8\\\omega^6&\omega^3&\omega^7\\\omega^8&\omega^7&1\end{vmatrix}$ is
en.explanation: With $\omega^3 = 1$ the determinant is $\begin{vmatrix}1&1&\omega^2\\1&1&\omega\\\omega^2&\omega&1\end{vmatrix} = 1(1 - \omega^2) - 1(1 - \omega^3) + \omega^2(\omega - \omega^2) = 1 - \omega^2 + 1 - \omega = 2 - (\omega + \omega^2) = 3$.
notes: Not zero: rows 1 and 2 differ in the last entry.
facts: Reduce powers of $\omega$ mod 3 first, then use $1 + \omega + \omega^2 = 0$.

en.q: The equation of the sphere on the join of $(2, -3, 1)$ and $(3, -1, 2)$ as diameter is
notes: Signs of the $z$-term and constant wrong.
facts: Sphere on the diameter AB: $(x - x_1)(x - x_2) + (y - y_1)(y - y_2) + (z - z_1)(z - z_2) = 0$.

en.q: A particle is projected with a velocity $u$ so that its range on a horizontal plane is twice the greatest height attained; the range is
en.explanation: $\dfrac{u^2\sin2\alpha}{g} = 2\cdot\dfrac{u^2\sin^2\alpha}{2g} \Rightarrow 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha = \sin^2\alpha \Rightarrow \tan\alpha = 2$. Then $\sin2\alpha = \dfrac{2\tan\alpha}{1 + \tan^2\alpha} = \dfrac45$, so $R = \dfrac{4u^2}{5g}$.
facts: $R = nH \Rightarrow \tan\alpha = \frac{4}{n}$.

en.q: The number of generators of a cyclic group of order 10 is
en.explanation: A cyclic group of order $n$ has $\varphi(n)$ generators; $\varphi(10) = 10\left(1 - \frac12\right)\left(1 - \frac15\right) = 4$ (namely $a, a^3, a^7, a^9$).
facts: Number of generators of a cyclic group of order $n$ is $\varphi(n)$.

en.q: The sequence $\left\langle \log\frac{1}{n} \right\rangle$ is
en.explanation: $\log\frac1n = -\log n$, and $\log n \to \infty$, so the terms decrease without bound: divergent to $-\infty$.
facts: $\log n \to \infty$ (slowly but without bound).

en.q: Solution of the differential equation $\log\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = ax + by$ is
en.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{ax}e^{by} \Rightarrow e^{-by}dy = e^{ax}dx \Rightarrow -\dfrac{e^{-by}}{b} = \dfrac{e^{ax}}{a} + c$. Multiply by $ab$: $be^{ax} + ae^{-by} + C = 0$.
facts: $\log y' = f(x) + g(y)$ separates as $e^{-g(y)}dy = e^{f(x)}dx$.

en.q: If $\lim_{x\to a}\frac{a^x - x^a}{x^x - a^a} = -1$, then
en.explanation: L'Hospital: $\dfrac{a^x\log a - ax^{a-1}}{x^x(1 + \log x)} \to \dfrac{a^a(\log a - 1)}{a^a(\log a + 1)} = -1 \Rightarrow \log a - 1 = -\log a - 1 \Rightarrow \log a = 0 \Rightarrow a = 1$.
facts: $\frac{d}{dx}a^x = a^x\log a$, $\frac{d}{dx}x^x = x^x(1 + \log x)$.

en.q: If $x$ is a real number, then the function $f(x) = x^3 + x^2 + x + 1$ has
en.explanation: $f'(x) = 3x^2 + 2x + 1$ has discriminant $4 - 12 < 0$, so $f'(x) > 0$ for all $x$: $f$ is strictly increasing, with no extremum.
facts: A cubic whose derivative has negative discriminant is monotonic.

en.q: The multiplicative group $\{1, -1, i, -i\}$ is a cyclic group, its generators are
en.explanation: Powers of $i$: $i, -1, -i, 1$, all four elements; so $i$ generates, and so does its inverse $-i$. $1$ and $-1$ have orders 1 and 2.
facts: If $a$ generates a cyclic group, so does $a^{-1}$.

en.q: The tangent to the curve $x = \dfrac{2at^2}{1 + t^2}$, $y = \dfrac{2at^3}{1 + t^2}$ at the point for which $t = \frac12$, is
en.explanation: $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{4at}{(1 + t^2)^2}$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{2a(3t^2 + t^4)}{(1 + t^2)^2}$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3t + t^3}{2} = \dfrac{13}{16}$ at $t = \frac12$. The point is $\left(\frac{2a}{5}, \frac{a}{5}\right)$. Tangent: $16y - \frac{16a}{5} = 13x - \frac{26a}{5} \Rightarrow 13x - 16y = 2a$.
facts: Parametric slope: $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}$.

en.q: $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 + \cdots + n^2}{n^3}$ is equal to
en.explanation: $\sum k^2 = \dfrac{n(n + 1)(2n + 1)}{6}$, so the ratio is $\dfrac{(1 + \frac1n)(2 + \frac1n)}{6} \to \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac13$. (Also $= \int_0^1 x^2dx$.)
path: 1.6 Sequences and series: AP, GP, HP

en.q: Distance between the straight lines $x + 2y = 5$ and $2x + 4y = 11$ is
en.explanation: Write the second as $x + 2y = \frac{11}{2}$. Distance $= \dfrac{|\frac{11}{2} - 5|}{\sqrt{1 + 4}} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt5}$.
notes: Takes $|11 - 10|/\sqrt5$ without first making the coefficients of $x, y$ equal.
facts: Parallel lines $ax + by = c_1$, $ax + by = c_2$: distance $\frac{|c_1 - c_2|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$ (same $a, b$ first).

en.q: If one zero of the third degree polynomial $x^3 + ax^2 + bx + c$ is $-1$, then the product of other two zeroes is
en.explanation: $p(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow -1 + a - b + c = 0 \Rightarrow c = 1 - a + b$. The product of all three zeros is $-c$; dividing by the zero $-1$ gives the product of the other two $= c = b - a + 1$.
path: 1.8 Quadratic equations and theory of equations
facts: Cubic $x^3 + ax^2 + bx + c$: $\alpha\beta\gamma = -c$.

en.q: The position vectors of the points A, B, C and D are $3\hat i - 2\hat j - \hat k$, $2\hat i + 3\hat j - 4\hat k$, $-\hat i + \hat j + 2\hat k$ and $4\hat i + 5\hat j + \lambda\hat k$ respectively. If the points A, B, C and D lie on a plane, the value of $\lambda$ is
en.explanation: $\overrightarrow{AB} = (-1, 5, -3)$, $\overrightarrow{AC} = (-4, 3, 3)$, $\overrightarrow{AD} = (1, 7, \lambda + 1)$. Coplanar $\iff$ $\begin{vmatrix}-1&5&-3\\-4&3&3\\1&7&\lambda+1\end{vmatrix} = 17\lambda + 146 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = -\frac{146}{17}$.
facts: Four points are coplanar iff the scalar triple product of the three edge vectors from one of them is 0.

en.q: If $x^2 + \dfrac{1}{x^2} = 11$, then value of $x^3 - \dfrac{1}{x^3}$ may be equal to
en.explanation: $\left(x - \frac1x\right)^2 = 11 - 2 = 9 \Rightarrow x - \frac1x = \pm3$. Then $x^3 - \frac{1}{x^3} = \left(x - \frac1x\right)^3 + 3\left(x - \frac1x\right) = 27 + 9 = 36$ (or $-36$).

en.q: If $(b - c)^2, (c - a)^2, (a - b)^2$ are in A.P., then $\dfrac{1}{b - c}, \dfrac{1}{c - a}, \dfrac{1}{a - b}$ will be in
en.explanation: Let $p = b - c$, $q = c - a$, $r = a - b$, so $p + q + r = 0$. $q^2 - p^2 = r^2 - q^2 \Rightarrow (q - p)(-r) = (r - q)(-p) \Rightarrow q(p + r) = 2pr \Rightarrow \dfrac2q = \dfrac1p + \dfrac1r$. So the reciprocals are in A.P.
notes: That would be true of $b - c, c - a, a - b$ themselves.
path: 1.6 Sequences and series: AP, GP, HP
facts: With $p + q + r = 0$: $p^2, q^2, r^2$ in A.P. $\iff$ $\frac1p, \frac1q, \frac1r$ in A.P.

en.q: A, B and C undertake to do a work for ₹ 500. A and B together do $\frac25$ of the work and rest is done by C alone. How much amount should C get?
en.explanation: C does $1 - \frac25 = \frac35$ of the work, so C gets $\frac35 \times 500 = 300$, i.e. ₹ 300.
notes: That is the share of A and B.
facts: Wages are shared in proportion to the work done.

en.q: $\left(\dfrac{1 + i}{\sqrt2}\right)^8 + \left(\dfrac{1 - i}{\sqrt2}\right)^8$ is equal to
en.explanation: $\dfrac{1 \pm i}{\sqrt2} = e^{\pm i\pi/4}$, so each eighth power is $e^{\pm 2\pi i} = 1$. Sum $= 2$.
path: 10.4 Polar form, Euler's form and De Moivre's theorem
facts: $\left(\frac{1 + i}{\sqrt2}\right)^2 = i$, so its 8th power is $i^4 = 1$.

en.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $a = 2b$ and $|A - B| = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$, then $\angle C$ is
en.explanation: Napier's analogy: $\tan\dfrac{A - B}{2} = \dfrac{a - b}{a + b}\cot\dfrac{C}{2}$. So $\tan\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{b}{3b}\cot\dfrac C2 \Rightarrow \cot\dfrac C2 = \sqrt3 \Rightarrow C = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
facts: Napier: $\tan\frac{A - B}{2} = \frac{a - b}{a + b}\cot\frac{C}{2}$.

en.q: The sides of a triangle are 15 cm, 20 cm and 25 cm respectively, then the radius of in-circle is
en.explanation: $15^2 + 20^2 = 25^2$, a right triangle. $\Delta = \frac12 \cdot 15 \cdot 20 = 150$, $s = 30$, $r = \frac{\Delta}{s} = 5$ cm.
notes: That is the circumradius (half the hypotenuse).
facts: $r = \Delta/s$; in a right triangle $r = \frac{a + b - c}{2}$.

en.q: The greatest resultant which two forces can have is $P$ and the least is $Q$. If they act at an angle $\alpha$, then the resultant is of magnitude
en.explanation: Forces $F_1 = \frac{P + Q}{2}$, $F_2 = \frac{P - Q}{2}$. $R^2 = F_1^2 + F_2^2 + 2F_1F_2\cos\alpha = \frac{P^2 + Q^2}{2} + \frac{P^2 - Q^2}{2}\cos\alpha = P^2\cos^2\frac{\alpha}{2} + Q^2\sin^2\frac{\alpha}{2}$.
facts: Greatest resultant = sum of the forces, least = their difference.

en.q: The work done in moving an object along a straight line from $(3, 2, -1)$ to $(2, -1, 4)$ in a force field given by $\vec F = 4\hat i - 3\hat j + 2\hat k$, is
en.explanation: Displacement $\vec d = (2 - 3, -1 - 2, 4 + 1) = (-1, -3, 5)$. $W = \vec F\cdot\vec d = -4 + 9 + 10 = 15$ units.
facts: Work by a constant force $= \vec F \cdot \vec d$.

en.q: If $\vec a, \vec b$ and $\vec c$ are three vectors in such a way that $\vec a + \vec b + \vec c = \vec 0$ and $|\vec a| = 1$, $|\vec b| = 4$, $|\vec c| = 2$, then the value of $2(\vec a\cdot\vec b + \vec b\cdot\vec c + \vec c\cdot\vec a)$ is equal to
en.explanation: $|\vec a + \vec b + \vec c|^2 = 0 = 1 + 16 + 4 + 2(\vec a\cdot\vec b + \vec b\cdot\vec c + \vec c\cdot\vec a)$, so the required value is $-21$. Note: the data are flawed. $\vec a + \vec b + \vec c = \vec 0$ forces $|\vec b| = |\vec a + \vec c| \le 1 + 2 = 3$, so no such vectors exist; $-21$ is what the intended identity gives.
notes: That is $\vec a\cdot\vec b + \vec b\cdot\vec c + \vec c\cdot\vec a$ without the factor 2.
facts: $|\vec a + \vec b + \vec c|^2 = \sum|\vec a|^2 + 2\sum\vec a\cdot\vec b$.

en.q: $\lim_{y\to a}\left(\sin\frac{y - a}{2}\cdot\tan\frac{\pi y}{2a}\right)$ is equal to
en.explanation: Put $y = a + h$, $h \to 0$. $\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + \frac{\pi h}{2a}\right) = -\cot\frac{\pi h}{2a} \approx -\frac{2a}{\pi h}$ and $\sin\frac h2 \approx \frac h2$. Product $\to -\frac{a}{\pi}$.
facts: Near $\frac{\pi}{2}$: $\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + t\right) = -\cot t$.

en.q: A particle is projected in vertically upward direction. If after $t_1$ and $t_2$ seconds, its height is $h$, then $h$ is equal to
en.explanation: $h = ut - \frac12gt^2$, i.e. $\frac12gt^2 - ut + h = 0$, has roots $t_1, t_2$. Product of roots: $t_1t_2 = \frac{2h}{g} \Rightarrow h = \frac12gt_1t_2$.
path: 15.8 Rectilinear motion and simple harmonic motion
facts: Also $u = \frac12 g(t_1 + t_2)$ from the sum of the roots.

en.q: The equation of the directrix of the parabola $y^2 + 4x + 4y + 2 = 0$ is
en.explanation: $(y + 2)^2 = -4x + 2 = -4\left(x - \frac12\right)$: vertex $\left(\frac12, -2\right)$, $a = 1$, opening left. Directrix: $x - \frac12 = 1$, i.e. $x = \frac32$.
notes: Directrix of $Y^2 = -4X$ without shifting the vertex to $x = \frac12$.
facts: For $Y^2 = -4aX$ the directrix is $X = a$.

en.q: The system of equations $x + z = 3$, $ax + y = 2$, $3x + y + bz = 7$ has a unique solution if $(a, b)$ is equal to
en.explanation: Unique solution $\iff \begin{vmatrix}1&0&1\\a&1&0\\3&1&b\end{vmatrix} = b + a - 3 \ne 0$. Only $(1, 1)$ gives $a + b \ne 3$.
path: 2.4 Rank and systems of linear equations
facts: $AX = B$ has a unique solution iff $|A| \ne 0$.

en.q: In a triangle ABC if $\cos A = \dfrac{\sin B}{2\sin C}$, then triangle is
en.explanation: $\cos A = \dfrac{b}{2c}$, and $\cos A = \dfrac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}$. So $b^2 = b^2 + c^2 - a^2 \Rightarrow a = c$: isosceles.
facts: Use the sine rule to turn sines into sides, then the cosine rule.

en.q: The equations of tangents to the ellipse $3x^2 + 4y^2 = 12$ which are parallel to the line $y + 2x = 4$ are
en.explanation: $\frac{x^2}{4} + \frac{y^2}{3} = 1$, slope $m = -2$. Tangent $y = mx \pm\sqrt{a^2m^2 + b^2} = -2x \pm\sqrt{16 + 3}$, i.e. $y + 2x = \pm\sqrt{19}$.
facts: $y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^2m^2 + b^2}$ touches $\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$.

en.q: If $\hat a$ and $\hat b$ are unit vectors such that $\hat a + 2\hat b$ and $5\hat a - 4\hat b$ are perpendicular to each other, then the angle between $\hat a$ and $\hat b$ is
en.explanation: $(\hat a + 2\hat b)\cdot(5\hat a - 4\hat b) = 5 - 4\hat a\cdot\hat b + 10\hat a\cdot\hat b - 8 = 6\hat a\cdot\hat b - 3 = 0 \Rightarrow \hat a\cdot\hat b = \frac12$, so the angle is $\frac{\pi}{3}$.
facts: For unit vectors $\hat a\cdot\hat b = \cos\theta$.

en.q: $\sin^{-1}\dfrac35 - \cos^{-1}\dfrac{12}{13}$ equals to
en.explanation: $\cos^{-1}\frac{12}{13} = \sin^{-1}\frac{5}{13}$. $\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \frac35\cdot\frac{12}{13} - \frac45\cdot\frac{5}{13} = \frac{36 - 20}{65} = \frac{16}{65}$; both angles are acute, so the answer is $\sin^{-1}\frac{16}{65}$.
facts: $\sin^{-1}x - \sin^{-1}y = \sin^{-1}\left(x\sqrt{1 - y^2} - y\sqrt{1 - x^2}\right)$ for $x, y \ge 0$.

en.q: For all $x \in (-1, 1)$, $\tanh^{-1}x$ is equal to
en.explanation: $y = \tanh^{-1}x \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{e^{2y} - 1}{e^{2y} + 1} \Rightarrow e^{2y} = \dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x} \Rightarrow y = \frac12\log\dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x}$.
path: 10.10 Inverse circular and inverse hyperbolic functions

en.q: $\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2 + 2\cos 8\theta}}}$ is equal to
en.explanation: Use $2 + 2\cos 2t = 4\cos^2 t$ three times (for small $\theta \ge 0$, all cosines positive): $\sqrt{2 + 2\cos8\theta} = 2\cos4\theta$, then $\sqrt{2 + 2\cos4\theta} = 2\cos2\theta$, then $\sqrt{2 + 2\cos2\theta} = 2\cos\theta$.
facts: $\sqrt{2 + 2\cos 2t} = 2|\cos t|$.

en.q: $\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sin x\cos x}{\cos^2x + 3\cos x + 2}\,dx$ is equal to
en.explanation: Put $t = \cos x$: $\int_0^1\frac{t\,dt}{(t + 1)(t + 2)} = \int_0^1\left(\frac{2}{t + 2} - \frac{1}{t + 1}\right)dt = \Big[2\log(t + 2) - \log(t + 1)\Big]_0^1 = 2\log3 - 3\log2 = \log\frac98$.

en.q: The mean weight of 9 items is 15 kg. If one more item is added then the mean weight becomes 16 kg, then the weight of tenth item will be
en.explanation: Old total $9 \times 15 = 135$; new total $10 \times 16 = 160$. The tenth item weighs $160 - 135 = 25$ kg.
facts: New item = new total − old total.

en.q: Two finite sets have $m$ and $n$ elements respectively. The number of subsets of the first set is greater than the number of the subsets of the second set by 56. Then the value of $m^2 + n^2$ is equal to
en.explanation: $2^m - 2^n = 56 \Rightarrow 2^n(2^{m-n} - 1) = 8 \times 7 \Rightarrow n = 3$, $m = 6$. Then $m^2 + n^2 = 36 + 9 = 45$, which is not listed.
facts: A set with $n$ elements has $2^n$ subsets.

en.q: In the following figure the value of $\theta$ is (figure: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral; T is outside the circle with T, S, P and T, R, Q collinear; $\angle PQR = 70^\circ$, $\angle SRQ = 130^\circ$, $\angle PTQ = \theta$)
en.explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral: $\angle P = 180^\circ - 130^\circ = 50^\circ$. In $\triangle TPQ$: $\theta = 180^\circ - 50^\circ - 70^\circ = 60^\circ$.
facts: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to $180^\circ$.

en.q: The intercept on the line $y = x$ by the circle $x^2 + y^2 - 2x = 0$ is AB. Equation of circle with AB as diameter is
en.explanation: $y = x$ in the circle: $2x^2 - 2x = 0 \Rightarrow A(0, 0), B(1, 1)$. Circle on AB as diameter: $x(x - 1) + y(y - 1) = 0$, i.e. $x^2 + y^2 - x - y = 0$.
facts: Circle on the diameter joining $(x_1, y_1), (x_2, y_2)$: $(x - x_1)(x - x_2) + (y - y_1)(y - y_2) = 0$.

en.q: Sequence $\log x, \log\dfrac{x^2}{y}, \log\dfrac{x^3}{y^2}, \dots$ is
en.explanation: The terms are $\log x$, $2\log x - \log y$, $3\log x - 2\log y$: each exceeds the previous by $\log x - \log y = \log\frac{x}{y}$. An A.P.
path: 1.6 Sequences and series: AP, GP, HP
facts: Logs of the terms of a G.P. form an A.P.

en.q: Ram can throw a ball vertically to a maximum height of 40 metres, then he can throw the ball in horizontal direction to which maximum distance?
en.explanation: Vertical throw: $u^2 = 2g \cdot 40 = 80g$. "In horizontal direction" is taken to mean along level ground. The greatest horizontal range with the same speed (at $45^\circ$) is $\frac{u^2}{g} = 80$ m.
facts: With a given speed, maximum range $= 2 \times$ maximum height $= \frac{u^2}{g}$.

en.q: If $f\left(x + \dfrac1x\right) = x^3 + \dfrac{1}{x^3}$, then $f(\sqrt3)$ is equal to
en.explanation: $x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = \left(x + \frac1x\right)^3 - 3\left(x + \frac1x\right)$, so $f(t) = t^3 - 3t$ and $f(\sqrt3) = 3\sqrt3 - 3\sqrt3 = 0$. Note: no real $x$ has $x + \frac1x = \sqrt3$ (for real $x$, $|x + \frac1x| \ge 2$). With complex $x = \cos\frac{\pi}{6} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{6}$ it holds, and $x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = 2\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0$, so the answer 0 stands.

en.q: If the mean of $x, x + 2, x + 4, x + 6, x + 8$ is 11, then what is the mean of the last three observations?
en.explanation: Mean $= x + 4 = 11 \Rightarrow x = 7$. Last three: $11, 13, 15$, mean $13$.
facts: Mean of an A.P. = its middle term.

en.q: Integral of $\int\frac{\cot x}{\log\sin x}\,dx$ is
en.explanation: Put $u = \log\sin x$, $du = \cot x\,dx$: $\int\frac{du}{u} = \log u + C = \log(\log\sin x) + C$.
facts: $\int\frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}dx = \log|f(x)| + C$.

en.q: If the mean of the observations 6, 8, 5, 7, $x$ and 4 is 7, then the median of these observations is
facts: For an even number of values the median is the mean of the two middle values.

en.q: Find the equation of the cone with vertex at the origin and direction cosines of its generators satisfy the equation $l^2 + 2m^2 - 3n^2 = 0$.
en.explanation: A point $(x, y, z)$ on a generator through O has $x : y : z = l : m : n$. Replacing $l, m, n$ by $x, y, z$ in the homogeneous relation gives $x^2 + 2y^2 - 3z^2 = 0$.
facts: A homogeneous relation in l, m, n becomes the cone by putting x, y, z for l, m, n.

en.q: Two parallel chords of a circle of radius 5 cm are in opposite side of the centre and if the chords are at distances 3 cm and 4 cm from the centre, then the difference of the lengths of the chords is
en.explanation: Lengths: $2\sqrt{25 - 9} = 8$ cm and $2\sqrt{25 - 16} = 6$ cm. Difference $= 2$ cm.
facts: Chord at distance $d$ from the centre: length $2\sqrt{r^2 - d^2}$.

en.q: If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are the roots of the equation $x^3 + px^2 + qx + r = 0$, then $\alpha^2\beta^2 + \alpha^2\gamma^2 + \beta^2\gamma^2$ is equal to
en.explanation: $\sum\alpha = -p$, $\sum\alpha\beta = q$, $\alpha\beta\gamma = -r$. $\sum\alpha^2\beta^2 = (\sum\alpha\beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta\gamma\sum\alpha = q^2 - 2(-r)(-p) = q^2 - 2pr$.
path: 1.8 Quadratic equations and theory of equations
facts: $\sum\alpha^2\beta^2 = (\sum\alpha\beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta\gamma\sum\alpha$.

en.q: Which one of the following is not a measure of central tendency?
en.explanation: Mean, median and mode locate the centre of the data; range measures its spread (dispersion).
notes: Correct: range is a measure of dispersion.
facts: Range, Q.D., M.D. and S.D. are measures of dispersion.

en.q: If $1, \omega, \omega^2$ are the cube roots of unity, then the value of $(1 + \omega^2)(1 + \omega^4)(1 + \omega^8)(1 + \omega^{16})$ is
en.explanation: $\omega^4 = \omega$, $\omega^8 = \omega^2$, $\omega^{16} = \omega$. Product $= (1 + \omega^2)^2(1 + \omega)^2 = (-\omega)^2(-\omega^2)^2 = \omega^6 = 1$.
path: 10.4 Polar form, Euler's form and De Moivre's theorem
facts: $1 + \omega = -\omega^2$ and $1 + \omega^2 = -\omega$.

en.q: $\int_0^1\frac{\tan^{-1}x}{1 + x^2}\,dx$ is equal to
en.explanation: Put $t = \tan^{-1}x$, $dt = \frac{dx}{1 + x^2}$: $\int_0^{\pi/4}t\,dt = \frac12\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{\pi^2}{32}$.

en.q: In the given figure O is the centre of the circle and $\angle AOB = 70^\circ$ then $70^\circ - x^\circ$ is equal to (figure: A, B, C on the circle, C on the major arc AB; chords CA and CB; $x^\circ = \angle ACB$)
en.explanation: The inscribed angle on arc AB is half the central angle: $x = \frac{70^\circ}{2} = 35^\circ$. So $70^\circ - x^\circ = 35^\circ$.
facts: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc.

en.q: For any two sets A and B, $A - (A - B)$ equals
en.explanation: $A - (A - B) = A \cap (A \cap B')' = A \cap (A' \cup B) = (A \cap A') \cup (A \cap B) = A \cap B$.
notes: Only the part of $B$ inside $A$ survives.
facts: $A - B = A \cap B'$.

en.q: Three numbers are chosen at random from numbers 1 to 15. The probability that they are consecutive is
en.explanation: Total choices $\binom{15}{3} = 455$. Consecutive triples $\{k, k + 1, k + 2\}$: $k = 1, \dots, 13$, so 13. $P = \frac{13}{455} = \frac{1}{35}$.
path: 16.1 Basic probability and the addition theorem
facts: From $1, \dots, n$ there are $n - 2$ sets of three consecutive numbers.

en.q: The co-ordinates of a moving point are $(2t^2 + 4, 4t + 6)$. Its locus will be
en.explanation: $t = \frac{y - 6}{4} \Rightarrow x - 4 = 2t^2 = \frac{(y - 6)^2}{8}$, i.e. $(y - 6)^2 = 8(x - 4)$: a parabola.
facts: $(at^2 + h, 2at + k)$ traces a parabola $(y - k)^2 = 4a(x - h)$.

en.q: If the equation $x^2 + y^2 + (c - 2)xy - 4x - 4y + c^2 = 0$ represents a circle, then its radius is
en.explanation: A circle has no $xy$ term: $c = 2$. Then $x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 4y + 4 = 0$, centre $(2, 2)$, radius $\sqrt{4 + 4 - 4} = 2$.
facts: Radius of $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ is $\sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}$.

en.q: In the figure $\angle A$ is equal to (figure: cyclic quadrilateral ABCD with $\angle A = (y + 10)^\circ$, $\angle B = (2x - 13)^\circ$, $\angle C = (3x + 11)^\circ$, $\angle D = (2y + 7)^\circ$)
en.explanation: $A + C = 180^\circ$: $3x + y = 159$. $B + D = 180^\circ$: $2x + 2y = 186 \Rightarrow x + y = 93$. So $x = 33$, $y = 60$, and $\angle A = y + 10 = 70^\circ$.
facts: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to $180^\circ$.

en.q: The function defined by $f(x) = \begin{cases}\frac{|x|}{x}, & x \ne 0\\ 0, & x = 0\end{cases}$ at $x = 0$ is
options: discontinuous at $x = 0$ and has discontinuity of first kind
discontinuous at $x = 0$ and has removable discontinuity
discontinuous at $x = 0$ and has discontinuity of second kind
en.explanation: $f(0^-) = -1$ and $f(0^+) = 1$: both one-sided limits exist but differ, a jump, i.e. a discontinuity of the first kind.
notes: Second kind needs a one-sided limit not to exist.
facts: First kind: both one-sided limits exist but are unequal (jump).

en.q: For any complex number $z$, the minimum value of $|z + 1| + |z - 2|$ is
en.explanation: $|z + 1| + |z - 2| = |z + 1| + |2 - z| \ge |(z + 1) + (2 - z)| = 3$, with equality for $z$ on the segment from $-1$ to $2$.
notes: A sum of moduli cannot be negative.
facts: $|z - a| + |z - b| \ge |a - b|$: the least distance sum is the distance between the points.

en.q: For all real $x$, the minimum value of $\dfrac{1 - x + x^2}{1 + x + x^2}$ is
en.explanation: Set $y = \frac{1 - x + x^2}{1 + x + x^2}$: $(y - 1)x^2 + (y + 1)x + (y - 1) = 0$. Real $x$ needs $(y + 1)^2 \ge 4(y - 1)^2 \Rightarrow 3y^2 - 10y + 3 \le 0 \Rightarrow \frac13 \le y \le 3$. Minimum $\frac13$ (at $x = 1$).
path: 1.8 Quadratic equations and theory of equations
facts: Range of a quadratic-over-quadratic: put it equal to $y$ and require the discriminant $\ge 0$.
